'''''Bauhinia forficata''''', commonly known as '''Brazilian orchid tree''',<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/st089|title=''Bauhinia forficata'': Brazilian Orchid-Tree|author=Edward F. Gilman and Dennis G. Watson|publisher=University of Florida|year=1993}}</ref> is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering]] [[tree]] in the [[pea]] family, [[Fabaceae]], that is native to South America.

== Taxonomy ==
''Bauhinia forficata'' was formally described by the German botanist [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link]]. It belongs to the genus ''[[Bauhinia]]'', a group comprising 187 species distributed throughout tropical regions of Africa, Asia, and South America. The species is a member of the [[Fabaceae]] family (also known as Leguminosae).<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Cechinel-Zanchett |first1=Camile Cecconi |last2=de Andrade |first2=Sérgio Faloni |last3=Cechinel-Filho |first3=Valdir |date=2018-07-01 |title=Ethnopharmacological, Phytochemical, Pharmacological and Toxicological Aspects of ''Bauhinia forficata'': A Mini-Review Covering the Last Five Years |journal=Natural Product Communications |language=EN |volume=13 |issue=7 |article-number=1934578X1801300732 |doi=10.1177/1934578X1801300732 |issn=1934-578X}}</ref> The epithet ''forficata'' refers to this forked or cleft leaf form.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=da Cunha |first1=A. M. |last2=Menon |first2=S. |last3=Menon |first3=R. |last4=Couto |first4=A. G. |last5=Bürger |first5=C. |last6=Biavatti |first6=M. W. |date=2010-01-01 |title=Hypoglycemic activity of dried extracts of Bauhinia forficata Link |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0944711309001676 |journal=Phytomedicine |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=37–41 |doi=10.1016/j.phymed.2009.06.007 |pmid=19577450 |issn=0944-7113|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Description ==
''Bauhinia forficata'' is a medium-sized broadleaf [[Evergreen|evergreen tree]] that typically reaches a height of {{Convert|25–30|ft}} with a [[Canopy (botany)|canopy]] spread ranging from {{Convert|25–35|ft}}. The species displays a symmetrical crown that may take on a vase-shaped, rounded, or spreading form, and has a dense canopy with a medium texture. Growth is moderate under suitable conditions.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Bauhinia forficata'' is native to South America.

In Brazil, its natural range extends from the state of [[Rio de Janeiro]] to [[Rio Grande do Sul]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pizzolatti |first1=Moacir Geraldo |last2=Cunha Jr. |first2=Anildo |last3=Szpoganicz |first3=Bruno |last4=Sousa |first4=Eliandra de |last5=Braz-Filho |first5=Raimundo |last6=Schripsema |first6=Jan |date=August 2003 |title=Flavonóides glicosilados das folhas e flores de Bauhinia forficata (Leguminosae) |journal=Química Nova |language=pt |volume=26 |issue=4 |pages=466–469 |doi=10.1590/S0100-40422003000400003 |issn=0100-4042|doi-access=free }}</ref> Within the country, it occurs in diverse ecosystems, including the semi-arid [[Caatinga]] region, forest fragments in the state of [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], and along the Amazon coastal areas.<ref name=":1" /> It is also native to other parts of the continent, including central and northern Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bauhinia forficata Link {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:481315-1 |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

It typically inhabits well-drained soils and performs best in full sun or areas with high, intermittent shade, such as beneath open pine canopies. Although it is tolerant of drought, the plant benefits from occasional irrigation or afternoon shade during hot, dry periods to prevent flower [[desiccation]]. In [[Alkali soil|alkaline soils]], it may exhibit interveinal [[chlorosis]] due to nutrient imbalances. ''Bauhinia forficata'' is suited to the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] (USDA) hardiness zones 10A through 11.<ref name=":0" />
